quick_skim.title: CRNDiff: Count-Native Diffusion Framework via Chemical Reaction Networks
quick_skim.abstract: Scientific measurements such as single-cell RNA (scRNA) sequencing often take the form of nonnegative integer counts, whereas continuous-state diffusion models approximate this discrete structure using continuous coordinates. Building on stochastic chemical reaction networks (CRNs), a class of count-native Markov jump processes, we introduce CRNDiff, a structured framework that combines count-space diffusion with inference-time conditioning on rare subpopulations. An independent birth--death instantiation yields a closed-form transition kernel for forward noising. This kernel enables reverse sampling via forward-filtering backward-sampling (FFBS) and supports data-driven selection of the terminal noising time, eliminating the need for a validation sweep. This tractability also lets us introduce tilted Feynman--Kac (FK) steering, a method for sampling target subpopulations from a frozen generator without retraining. By tilting posterior marginals before FK particle correction, steering mitigates importance-weight concentration when the target population is rare. Using scRNA-seq data from the human heart cell atlas, we test the ability of CRNDiff to generate cell-type-specific distributions. Across the three evaluated target populations, CRNDiff achieves the highest conditional fidelity among the evaluated generative models, with larger mean purity margins for rarer target populations. Generated cells preserve marker-level differential-expression structure. Replacing real training cells for the target classes with generated cells yields downstream classification performance approaching that of the real-data reference.

quick_skim.llm_tldr_en: Continuous diffusion models approximate discrete single-cell counts poorly. CRNDiff uses chemical reaction networks for count-native diffusion with inference-time conditioning, enabling closed-form noising and FFBS sampling for rare subpopulations.
quick_skim.llm_tldr_cn: 单细胞RNA测序等科学测量本质上是非负整数计数，而连续状态扩散模型却用连续坐标近似这一离散结构，造成建模偏差。本文提出CRNDiff，基于随机化学反应网络这一计数原生马尔可夫跳过程，将计数空间扩散与推断时的稀有亚群条件化相结合；独立生灭过程实例给出前向加噪的闭式转移核，从而支持前向滤波后向采样与终端加噪时间的数据驱动选择。该框架为单细胞计数数据提供了更贴合其离散本质的生成建模途径，有望服务于虚拟细胞与扰动响应预测等下游任务。
